outputs.L4:
The method provides a gesture-based technique for editing or deleting items displayed in a list or similar content arrangement. A user first performs a drag gesture in a direction substantially orthogonal to the list’s primary scrolling direction. For example, if the list scrolls vertically, the user may drag horizontally across an item. This initial movement selects or activates the item without interfering with ordinary list navigation.

After selecting the item, the user reverses the direction of the drag while maintaining the gesture. The reverse movement changes the item’s state and marks it for deletion, which may be indicated visually through highlighting, displacement, animation, or a deletion symbol. If the user completes the prescribed gesture, the system deletes the marked item. If the gesture is canceled or does not pass the required threshold, the item can return to its original state, reducing the risk of accidental deletion.

The same interaction model may also be used for editing rather than deletion. Drag distance, direction, position, or duration can control one or more parameters associated with the selected item. The gesture may extend across multiple content items, allowing the user to select several items and apply the same or related parameter changes to them simultaneously. In this way, the method supports fast, direct manipulation of list content while preserving the conventional scrolling behavior of the interface.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a patent describing gesture-based deletion and simultaneous parameter editing of items in a displayed list.
counterfactuals.output:
The patent describes a graphical user interface for managing items in an on-screen list using touch or pointer gestures. A user can delete an item by performing a designated gesture—such as swiping or dragging the item toward a deletion area—rather than opening menus or confirmation dialogs. The interface also allows multiple list items to be selected or manipulated together so that a shared parameter, such as a value, status, setting, or position, can be changed simultaneously.

The invention’s main purpose is to make list management faster and more intuitive by combining direct gesture-based deletion with coordinated bulk editing. Its claims likely cover detecting the gestures, identifying the affected items, updating the underlying data, and visually reflecting the deletion or parameter changes on the display.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft patent-style language for a touch interface that lets users delete or simultaneously edit list items through a continuous back-and-forth swipe gesture.
counterfactuals.output:
## Title

**Continuous Bidirectional Swipe Gesture for Deleting or Concurrently Editing List Items**

## Abstract

A touch-interface system receives a continuous touch gesture traversing a displayed list of items. While contact with the touch surface is maintained, the gesture may reverse direction one or more times and intersect, cross, or otherwise designate multiple list items. The system maintains a selection set based on the items designated during the continuous gesture and, in response to completion of the gesture or satisfaction of an execution criterion, performs a common operation on the selection set. The common operation may include deleting the designated items or concurrently modifying one or more properties of the designated items. Direction reversals, traversal distance, dwell time, pressure, velocity, or an initially contacted control region may be used to distinguish the gesture from scrolling and to select an applicable operation.

## Example Specification Language

A computing device may provide a graphical user interface including a plurality of items arranged as a list. The computing device may detect a continuous touch input beginning at a first location and moving across at least a portion of the list while contact with a touch-sensitive surface is maintained. The continuous touch input may include at least one reversal in direction, such that the input follows a back-and-forth path over respective portions of the list.

As the path traverses the list, the computing device may identify list items intersected by the path, entered by a contact indicator, crossed by a selection boundary, or otherwise designated according to a spatial relationship between the path and the displayed items. The identified items may be added to a temporary selection set. In some implementations, a subsequent traversal of an item during the same continuous touch input toggles the selection state of the item. In other implementations, once designated, an item remains in the selection set until the touch input terminates or the path satisfies a removal criterion.

Visual feedback may be presented during the gesture. For example, designated items may be highlighted, displaced, partially collapsed, marked with a deletion indicator, or displayed with a preview of a proposed edit. The visual feedback may be updated dynamically as the contact moves and reverses direction.

Upon detecting termination of the continuous touch input, passage through an execution region, expiration of a dwell interval, or satisfaction of another execution condition, the computing device may perform a common action with respect to each item in the selection set. The common action may include deletion, archival, movement, categorization, assignment of a shared attribute, modification of a shared field, or application of a common value. The action may be performed as a single transaction so that the selected items are updated together and, optionally, may be restored together by an undo operation.

To distinguish the continuous back-and-forth gesture from a scrolling gesture, the computing device may evaluate one or more of: an initial touch location; a predominantly lateral component of movement relative to the list axis; a number of direction reversals; a reversal angle; traversal of an item-control region; touch pressure; contact area; movement velocity; or a duration of the input. The list may remain stationary during the gesture, or may automatically scroll when the touch location approaches an edge of a display.

## Example Claims

1. **A computer-implemented method comprising:**  
   displaying, by a computing device having a touch-sensitive interface, a plurality of items in a list;  
   detecting a continuous touch gesture that traverses portions of two or more of the items while contact with the touch-sensitive interface is maintained, the continuous touch gesture including at least one reversal of movement direction;  
   during the continuous touch gesture, identifying a set of the items based on a path of the continuous touch gesture relative to the displayed items;  
   presenting visual feedback indicating membership of respective items in the set; and  
   in response to detecting an execution condition associated with the continuous touch gesture, applying a common operation to the set of items.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the common operation comprises deleting each item in the set.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the common operation comprises concurrently modifying a common property of each item in the set.

4. The method of claim 3, wherein concurrently modifying the common property comprises applying a shared value, category, status, destination, priority, date, permission, or formatting attribute to each item in the set.

5. The method of claim 1, wherein identifying the set comprises adding an item to the set when the path enters or crosses a displayed region corresponding to the item.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein identifying the set comprises toggling a membership state of an item each time the path traverses a designated region of the item.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein an item added to the set remains in the set notwithstanding a subsequent traversal of the item during the continuous touch gesture.

8. The method of claim 1, wherein the execution condition comprises termination of contact with the touch-sensitive interface.

9. The method of claim 1, wherein the execution condition comprises movement of the continuous touch gesture into a displayed execution region while contact is maintained.

10. The method of claim 1, further comprising distinguishing the continuous touch gesture from a list-scrolling gesture based on at least one of an initial touch location, a direction of initial movement, a movement distance, a direction-reversal count, a reversal angle, a velocity, a pressure, a contact area, or a gesture duration.

11. The method of claim 1, wherein the visual feedback comprises dynamically displaying, before application of the common operation, a preview of an effect of the common operation on each item in the set.

12. The method of claim 1, further comprising automatically scrolling the list when a contact location associated with the continuous touch gesture is maintained within an edge region of a display.

13. The method of claim 1, wherein applying the common operation comprises applying the common operation to the set as an atomic transaction.

14. The method of claim 13, further comprising receiving an undo input and, responsive thereto, reversing the common operation for the set as a group.

15. **A computing device comprising:**  
   a touch-sensitive display;  
   one or more processors; and  
   memory storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the computing device to:  
   display a list comprising a plurality of items;  
   track a continuous touch path extending over multiple items and including a back-and-forth change in movement direction;  
   maintain, while the continuous touch path is being tracked, a collection of items designated by the continuous touch path; and  
   responsive to completion of the continuous touch path, delete the designated items or apply a shared edit to the designated items.

16. The computing device of claim 15, wherein the instructions further cause the computing device to update the collection in real time as the continuous touch path enters respective item regions.

17. The computing device of claim 15, wherein the instructions further cause the computing device to determine whether to delete the designated items or apply the shared edit based on a control region at which the continuous touch path begins, ends, or reverses direction.

18. The computing device of claim 15, wherein the shared edit is specified by a value selected before, during, or after the continuous touch path.

19. **A non-transitory computer-readable medium** storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors of a touch-enabled computing device, cause the computing device to:  
   detect a continuous contact moving in a first direction across a list and subsequently moving in a second, opposing direction without loss of contact;  
   designate multiple list items according to intersections between the continuous contact and respective regions associated with the multiple list items; and  
   execute, for the designated multiple list items, a group deletion operation or a group editing operation.

20. The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 19, wherein the instructions further cause the computing device to suppress scrolling of the list after determining that the continuous contact satisfies a bidirectional-selection criterion.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
